text: Eleven down. The other eleven are one-liners, so here they come. To find duplicate rows, group by the columns that should be unique, and keep the counts over one. To see every copy, number them, and keep the numbers over one. A subquery nests a step inside the query. Written as a CTE, the step gets a name up front, reads top to bottom, and can be used twice. Here, both find the same three users. UNION stacks two results and removes duplicates, which costs a sort or a hash. UNION ALL keeps every row, so prefer it unless you need the dedup. Lag reads a value from an earlier row, and lead from a later one. Revenue minus lag is the change since yesterday, with no self join. At the edges there's no row to read: null, unless you pass a default, like this zero. A running total is a sum ordered by date, framed from the first row to this one, per user. Leave the frame out, and the default is range, so rows tied on a date share one total. To pivot, sum a case expression for each new column, grouped by the row. DuckDB also has a pivot clause. If the values aren't known in advance, it takes dynamic sequel. An inner join keeps only matches: six rows. Left keeps every customer, so Di comes back with nulls. Right keeps every order, the stray one too. Full keeps both: eight. N tile deals ordered rows into N buckets: twenty-four customers make four quartiles of six. When it can't split evenly, the first buckets get the extra rows. Percent rank is rank minus one, over rows minus one. Cume dist is the share of rows at or tied with this one. For ten, twenty, twenty, thirty, the twenties get a third, and three quarters. Coalesce returns its first argument that isn't null: the phone, else the email, else no contact. Null if goes the other way, turning a zero divisor into a null. And a cross join pairs every row with every row: three products by four regions make twelve. Use it on purpose, for a planning grid or a date-by-segment spine. Every table here held a few dozen rows. The same queries get harder when the table is too big to scan. Next: sequel performance.
